title: Decem Theses III-IV: One Confession in two exemplars; Formula Concord insert differs in words, not substance
pass_a_gloss: III. Those two exemplars contain not a twofold, but one and the same Confession, nor does the later differ from the earlier in the substantial articles of faith, but only in words and in a clearer explanation. IV. The exemplar of the Augsburg Confession inserted into the Formula of Concord is indeed in certain words diverse from that which, printed at Wittenberg in the Year 31, is found in Luther's Tomes; yet in substantial matters it fully agrees with the same.
pass_b_english: III. Those two exemplars are not two confessions, but one and the same: the later differs from the earlier not in the substance of the faith's articles, but only in wording and clearer explanation.
IV. The Augsburg Confession text slotted into the Formula of Concord does differ in some words from the 1531 Wittenberg printing in Luther's volumes; in substance, though, it fully matches that text.
source_text:
III.
Duo illa exemplaria, non duplicem, sed unam eandemq; Confessionem continent, nec posterius à priori, substantialibus fidei articulis, sed solis verbis clariorique explicatione, differt.
IV.
Exemplar Augustanae Confessionis, Formulae Concordiae insertum, in quibusdam quidem verbis, ab eo, quod Wittebergae An. 31. impressum in Tomis Lutheri invenitur, est diversum; in substantialibus tamen plenè cum eodem convenit.
